Useful after config changes (e.g. switching embedding model or

The ``session_id`` is extracted from the authenticated session

get.description:
Detect orphaned data between the metadata DB and vector store.

Returns a consistency report with:
- ``db_only``: Documents in the DB but missing from the vector store
  (likely a failed ingestion).
- ``vec_only``: Chunks in the vector store with no DB record
  (likely a leaked vector after a hard-delete failure).
- ``collections``: the collections scanned, one per embedding model.
- ``scan_limited``: True if the vector scan hit ``vector_scan_limit``.
- ``incomplete``/``incomplete_reason``: the vector scan failed or hit the
  limit, so no orphans are reported (a document the scan did not reach is
  not missing) and repair refuses to run.

This endpoint is **read-only**: it does not modify any data.
Pass the report to ``POST /admin/gc/repair`` to fix the issues.

post.description:
Trigger a manual full garbage-collection cycle.

Runs all 7 GC phases:

0. Fail documents still processing long after any worker could be on them
1. Hard-delete expired soft-deleted documents
2. Expire documents past their TTL
3. Clean up old ERROR documents
4. Clean up expired citations
5. Clean up idle sessions
6. Reconcile quota counters

Idempotent: safe to call multiple times.  Returns per-phase results.

post.description:
Upload multiple documents in a single request.

Files are processed concurrently up to the configured
``max_concurrent_uploads`` limit.  Each file goes through the same
pipeline as the single-upload endpoint (text extraction, chunking,
embedding, vector indexing). Without Celery, a file that finds every
processing thread busy waits for one to free up (at most
``processing_timeout`` seconds), so a batch larger than the pool is
processed in full; the response returns once every file is accepted.

A batch may hold at most ``RAG_MAX_BATCH_FILES`` files (default 20) and
``RAG_MAX_BATCH_BYTES`` in total (default 200 MiB, refused with 413 before
the body is read).

post.description:
Soft-delete (archive) a document.

The document is marked as ``soft_deleted`` and enters the GC grace window.
Vectors and the stored file are **not** removed immediately: the GC
hard-deletes them after the configured grace period (default: 24 h).

Use ``POST /{document_id}/restore`` to recover the document before the
grace window expires.

Unlike ``DELETE /{document_id}``, this operation is **reversible**.

post.description:
Create a signed session token encoding (session_id, user_id).

The token is self-contained: the server decodes it on each request
without any database lookup.  Pass it via the ``X-Session-Token``
header on subsequent requests.

Both ``session_id`` and ``user_id`` are optional and are generated when
omitted, which is the normal path and needs no credentials.

**Naming them requires ``X-Admin-Token``.** Without that check this endpoint
hands out a token for any identity the caller asks for, and since sessions
are the isolation boundary, that is read/write access to another tenant's
documents. Requested identities are therefore refused rather than silently
replaced with generated ones: quietly returning a different session than
the one asked for would look like success and fail later in a confusing
place.

**With ``RAG_REQUIRE_AUTH`` on, an ``X-API-Key`` from ``RAG_API_KEYS`` is
required** (or ``X-Admin-Token``). The key's principal is written into the
token, and rate limits are counted per principal rather than per session.

401.description: Auth is on and X-API-Key is missing or wrong

403.description: Naming a session_id or user_id needs X-Admin-Token
